worktree_state: Pre-existing dirty/untracked work preserved. This activity added/updated its evidence report and architecture documentation; no commit or push was made.
scope: Recheck the current PRoot checkout and live native access before Wake Lock or SSH implementation.
Use the existing authenticated native SSH session for read-only inspection and owner-authorized isolated xgo launch/stop; no SSH/boot/service configuration was changed.
Do not change any Ternux repository, PRoot launcher, SSH service, boot policy, or Wake Lock state.

tests.component: Native SSH access to Ternuxx checkout
tests.environment: PRoot Debian SSH client to Android loopback port 8022
tests.test_case: Batch-mode authentication to the existing endpoint
tests.method: Read-only SSH command with a five-second connection timeout
tests.expected: Authenticated access to the native checkout and diagnostics
tests.actual: An authenticated read-only command reached the native checkout and returned its Git identity/status. The initial BatchMode probe was not a valid password-authentication test.
tests.evidence: Authenticated SSH command reported native checkout /data/data/com.termux/files/home/ternuxx, commit 1a891faabc925136c1801f40194b0969d28041df, and preserved dirty/untracked paths.
tests.uncertainty: The native checkout origin still names soobujmiah/ternuxx.git while the PRoot checkout names soobujmiah/ternuxx.git. Both report the same HEAD; their dirty worktrees differ. The initial SSH probe used StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new and host-key records were not independently pinned before a subsequent authenticated attempt.

tests.environment: Android shell via connected ADB device authorized local ADB observation (model [redacted device serial])
tests.test_case: Observe TCP listeners on the configured SSH port
tests.expected: Report observed bind addresses without inferring reachability
tests.actual: ADB shell showed listeners on 0.0.0.0:8022 and *:8022 without process attribution. The native Ternuxx SSH diagnostic could not read either TCP procfs table and reported listener observation unavailable.
tests.evidence: Live `ss -ltnp` output from adb shell plus `ternuxx ssh inspect --json` over authenticated SSH
tests.uncertainty: Listener ownership, effective sshd configuration, and external network reachability remain unverified.

tests.test_case: Inspect package presence and receiver metadata
tests.method: Read-only `pm path` and filtered `dumpsys package com.termux.boot` queries
tests.expected: Determine whether the app is present; do not equate package presence with successful boot execution
tests.actual: Package path and BootReceiver/RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED metadata were present. Package state reported stopped=true and enabled=0 (default). Native `ternuxx boot status --json` reported app=unknown, command unavailable, startup policy unknown, and one regular script in the boot directory. No boot-script execution was verified.
tests.evidence: Live ADB package-manager output, native boot status JSON, and a filename/permission-only listing of the boot directory
tests.uncertainty: Whether the owner has opened/initialized the app, whether its receiver runs on the next boot, and whether the current boot hook executes are unknown.

tests.component: Termux Wake Lock ownership and PRoot launcher cleanup
tests.environment: Native Termux and existing Ternux PRoot launcher
tests.test_case: Inspect acquisition, release, and ownership semantics before migration
tests.method: Repository baseline review only; no native shell or launcher file access
tests.expected: Verify live launcher ownership before any change
tests.actual: Live `x.sh` requests `termux-wake-lock` at startup and `termux-wake-unlock` in EXIT cleanup. Android PowerManager reported the app-global `termux:service-wakelock` active before and after the xgo test; its owner cannot be attributed to a workload.
tests.evidence: Native `x.sh` read over authenticated SSH; Android `dumpsys power` observations before, during, and after xgo; `termux-wake-lock` and `termux-wake-unlock` commands were available.
tests.uncertainty: The Termux mechanism is app-global and no per-service owner is exposed by these observations. The active lock's originating workload and whether x.sh's unlock released/reacquired it remain unknown. The original launcher was not edited.

tests.environment: Native Termux launcher plus a separate Debian PRoot/X11 session
tests.test_case: Launch xgo with no pre-existing desktop session; verify the new desktop and cleanly stop it
tests.method: Owner-authorized `bash -ic xgo` over authenticated SSH; inspect X11 windows and Android processes; send Ctrl-C to the test SSH PTY
tests.expected: New Xfce session appears and can be stopped without terminating the agent's existing PRoot or native SSH
tests.actual: Termux:X11 :0, PulseAudio, xfce4-session, xfwm4, panel windows, and a Thunar window appeared. Ctrl-C ended the new session with status 130. Follow-up process checks showed the new X11/XFCE/PulseAudio processes gone while sshd and the pre-existing PRoot PID 30131 remained.
tests.evidence: X11 `xdpyinfo`, `xwininfo -root -tree`, `xdotool` panel-window IDs, ADB process lists before/during/after, and an authenticated post-xgo SSH command.
tests.uncertainty: This verifies launch/process lifecycle, not visual quality or audio functionality. XFCE emitted expected PRoot limitations/warnings for systemd proxy, DBus, DPMS, colord, and power state. `xgo` still invokes broad process/socket cleanup and global Wake Lock commands.

tests.test_case: Create and verify a recoverable x.sh backup before any launcher change
tests.method: Owner-requested `cp -p`, byte comparison, SHA-256, and mode/size checks over authenticated SSH
tests.expected: A private backup exactly matches the original launcher; original remains untouched
tests.actual: Backup `~/x.sh.ternuxx-backup-20261017T163623Z` matches source SHA-256 `196edaa59a8e7990198781a3551058b0c29d67961bad47d816102374fe90734a`, mode 700, 2507 bytes. Original x.sh was not edited.
tests.uncertainty: The backup is in native Termux private home and is not a Git-managed rollback artifact. No launcher patch has been applied.

tests.component: Native SSH and pre-existing PRoot after xgo cleanup
tests.environment: Android device observed through ADB and authenticated SSH
tests.test_case: Verify current sshd/listener and original PRoot remain after stopping the newly launched GUI session
tests.method: Read-only process/listener inspection and a fresh authenticated SSH diagnostic command
tests.expected: Existing native SSH and PRoot continue while only xgo's new GUI session exits
tests.actual: sshd PID 11957 and port 8022 listeners remained; pre-existing PRoot PID 30131 remained; the new GUI/X11 processes stopped; fresh authenticated SSH command succeeded.
tests.evidence: ADB process/socket output and authenticated post-xgo SSH output
tests.uncertainty: The wildcard listener remains; listener ownership and external network reachability are not established. This is not a reboot-independence test.

tests.expected: Existing tests pass without changing device state
tests.evidence: Captured test runner output in the active implementation session
tests.uncertainty: This suite is host-side unit/mock evidence and does not verify installation or Android Wake Lock/boot behavior.

tests.test_case: Check for existing runit/termux-services supervisor without changing packages
tests.method: Read-only `command -v sv` and installed-package query; native SSH diagnostic service-supervisor field
tests.expected: Identify an existing supervisor before adding another
tests.actual: `sv` and `termux-services` were not detected; `ternuxx ssh inspect` reported service_supervisor=not_detected.
tests.evidence: Native command/package inspection and SSH diagnostic JSON
tests.uncertainty: A nonstandard supervisor or manually managed service may exist; no broad process or filesystem scan was performed.

rollback.device_configuration_changed: No SSH/boot/service configuration was changed. A byte-identical x.sh backup was created and the existing xgo workflow was started/stopped. The original x.sh remains unchanged.
rollback.ssh_known_hosts_note: The initial SSH probe used StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new; matching host-key records are present and may have been added by that attempt. The subsequent password-authenticated command used StrictHostKeyChecking=yes. The fingerprint was not independently pinned against the native host key before authentication.
rollback.user_action: Verify the [127.0.0.1]:8022 known-host fingerprint against a trusted native fingerprint before relying on future password-authenticated connections. The records were not deleted.
